**Given:** AC, the exact positive incidence/reality convention, the full framed unitary ASD and Ward objects in the Statement, and the absolute GAGA interface. Only that existing supplier's unresolved analytic package remains conditional here.

[A1] Absolute projective GAGA supplies the exact coherent tensor equivalence and cohomology comparison. Its five analytic prerequisite packages and full projective generation proof remain authoring obligations. The relative-family comparison map is constructed in its current proof and is not a separate assumed theorem. [[thm-qftx-projective-gaga-for-monad-data]]

[F1] Positive stereographic orientation, incidence equations, the involution and the pairing-induced positive Hermitian form have their exact local definition. [[def-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-and-twistor-data]]

[F2] A square-zero smooth Dolbeault operator on a finite-rank bundle has local holomorphic frames, and intertwining maps are holomorphic. [[lem-qftx-local-integrable-dolbeault-frames]]

[F3] Absolute GAGA, algebraic line-family cohomology/base change and the elementary local P¹ product argument give the actual analytic section bundle and evaluation isomorphism near every real line; surjectivity is proved, not assumed. The scalar O(-1) degree-zero and degree-one groups vanish. [[lem-qftx-twistor-line-section-direct-image]], [[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]]

[F4] Framed unitary ASD determinant reduction and the exact trace Chern-Weil normalization give q_N=-c₂[S⁴]. [[lem-qftx-u-n-determinant-flat-charge-normalization]]

[F5] The normal Thom class represents the oriented Poincaré dual, and integral projective cohomology is generated by the tautological Euler class; its negative is c₁(O(1)). [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]], [[lem-integral-cohomology-ring-of-complex-projective-space-by-splitting]]



**Given:** The stated objects and the single conditional supplier [A1].

1.1 In the chart w=λ₂/λ₁ on a real incidence fiber, the projected horizontal (0,1) directions are H₁=∂bar_z₁−w∂z₂ and H₂=∂bar_z₂+w∂z₁. Indeed these and the vertical ∂bar_w annihilate the holomorphic coordinates w, μ₁=z₁−bar_z₂w, μ₂=z₂+bar_z₁w. They are independent and commute; their coefficients are holomorphic in w. For a unitary connection A define the pulled-back (0,1) operator by the vertical ordinary derivative and ∇_A along H₁,H₂. Its mixed squares vanish by the displayed commuting generators and holomorphic w coefficients. Its horizontal square is F_A(H₁,H₂)=F_bar1bar2−w(F_1bar1+F_2bar2)+w²F_12, which vanishes for an ASD two-form in the positive orientation: the three coefficients are precisely its self-dual component. Thus the operator squares to zero on this chart, and on the other projective chart by the same tensorial calculation. Apply [F2] to obtain a genuine holomorphic bundle. Its restriction to every real line is the constant bundle E_x, with positive reality pairing induced by the unitary metric and framing at infinity. This pairing is holomorphic: its vertical derivative vanishes on the constant fibres, and differentiating horizontally gives zero by the original identity ∇_A h=0, with the conjugate pullback at σ interchanging the conjugate horizontal directions. [F1, F2, construct, algebra]

2.1 For any Ward bundle use [F3] to form the analytic vector bundle H over a complex-open neighborhood U of every real line in G=Gr(2,4), with holomorphic evaluation p*H≅e*E on the universal family. On a graph chart X:A→B, incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ]. The distribution D=ker(de) consists of matrix variations v with vλ=0 and no λ variation. It is a holomorphic involutive rank-two subbundle, since it is tangent to the fibers of the submersion e. The restriction of p*Ω¹_U to D has kernel B*⊗O(-1) on each projective-line fiber and target D*≅O(1)². The O(-1) vanishings in [F3] give Ω¹_U≅p_*D*. Equivalently, on the graph chart a linear covector on Hom(A,B) restricts to a section on all kernels vλ=0; the map is injective because those kernels span Hom(A,B), and both coefficient spaces have dimension four. This gives the holomorphic sheaf isomorphism without any extra analytic base-change assumption. [A1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The bundle e*E has a canonical flat partial connection δ along D: in a holomorphic frame pulled back from E, differentiate coefficient functions along the fibers of e. Changes of that frame have zero D derivative, so δ is well-defined and flat. Transfer δ to p*H by evaluation. For a local holomorphic section s of H, δ(p*s) is a section of D*⊗p*H. Push down using Ω¹_U≅p_*D* from step 2.1 to define ∇s. The partial Leibniz rule becomes ∇(fs)=df⊗s+f∇s, so ∇ is a holomorphic full connection. Its pullback restriction to D is δ, first on pulled-back sections and then on all sections by Leibniz. It is unique: the difference of two such connections is an End(H)-valued one-form restricting to zero on D at every λ, hence zero by the same cotangent isomorphism. The curvature restricts on D to δ²=0. Connections on overlapping graph charts agree by uniqueness. [F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Restrict H and ∇ to the totally real graph locus M=HP¹. Its smooth real incidence is diffeomorphic to Z by (P,[v])↦[v], with inverse [v]↦(span(v,jv),[v]); the explicit charts in [F3] verify smoothness. Under this identification dp(D) is exactly the span of H₁,H₂ in step 1.1: write X_z=((z₁,-bar_z₂),(z₂,bar_z₁)) and solve v(1,w)^T=0. Therefore the restricted smooth connection has F(H₁,H₂)=0 for every w, so all three self-dual coefficients in step 1.1 vanish. Hence it is ASD. Evaluation intertwines the original holomorphic operator on E with the reconstructed vertical/horizontal Dolbeault operator: it is holomorphic vertically, and on D its derivative is exactly the canonical relative derivative δ by step 3.1. These directions generate the (0,1) tangent in step 1.1, proving equality of the full operators, not just of underlying bundles. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 To identify the connection with the first-neighborhood prescription, the line's conormal bundle is O(-1)², by its two independent linear defining equations. The sequence 0→E|L⊗(I/I²)→E|L^(1)→E|L→0 and [F3]'s O(-1) vanishings give a unique extension of every line section to L^(1). Smooth variation is supplied by step 3.1, not merely inferred from this pointwise uniqueness. At a graph X choose a local holomorphic section s of H with specified value and ∇s(X)=0; in a local frame its affine-linear coefficient function can realize any prescribed first jet. Its evaluation derivative in parameter direction v vanishes on vλ=0 by step 3.1, so factors through the normal displacement vλ. These factorizations glue on the two λ charts and give precisely a first-neighborhood extension. Uniqueness identifies it with the preceding extension. Subtracting such a horizontal first jet from an arbitrary section shows that differentiation relative to this extension is exactly ∇. This proves the prescription, its Leibniz rule, chart independence and smooth dependence. [F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 The section metric is the form induced by b_z(s(z),t(σz)) in [F1]. It is independent of z on each line because that scalar is holomorphic on P¹, and is smooth by the evaluation frames of [F3]. The preceding construction commutes with duals, conjugate pullback and bundle morphisms: each commutes with the canonical relative e-connection and the cotangent isomorphism, and uniqueness in step 3.1 then forces the full connections to commute. Apply this to the holomorphic reality isomorphism E→σ*bar_E*. On the real line locus, the induced conjugate involution fixes the parameter and its real tangent vectors. Thus the induced map H→bar_H* intertwines ∇ with the conjugate dual connection, which is precisely X h(s,t)=h(∇_X s,t)+h(s,∇_X t) for real X. Positivity from [F1] makes ∇ unitary. Arbitrary independent positive forms would not satisfy this identity and are not used. [F1, F3, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Starting from A in step 1.1, its constant real-line sections identify the reconstructed smooth H with E. Along every alpha-plane the recovered connection has the same derivative as A; the cotangent uniqueness in step 3.1 makes the full connections equal. The unitary reality pairing and framing also agree. Starting from a Ward bundle, step 4.1 proves evaluation is a holomorphic isomorphism from the reconstructed pullback to the original bundle, and step 5.2 preserves its reality pairing and metric. These constructions and identities apply to morphisms as well, so descend to inverse maps on based unitary gauge and framed holomorphic isomorphism classes. No irreducibility or absence of parallel sections was used. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.2, algebra]

7.1 The explicit incidence chart fixes vertical complex orientation followed by the positive base orientation to be the complex orientation of Z. The pullback of the positive point Thom class on S⁴ is the positive normal Thom class of its fiber CP¹; [F5] identifies its absolute class as the Poincaré dual of that fiber. A linear CP¹ has dual H²: H restricts with integral one to the line, and the integral projective cohomology ring gives H² as its positive degree-four generator. Hence π*u=H² for the positive generator u of H⁴(S⁴). Smooth evaluation gives E_twistor≅π*H, so c₂(E_twistor)=kH² is equivalent to c₂(H)[S⁴]=k. By [F4] this is q_N=-k; the same calculation verifies the forward map's charge clause. Framing is transported by evaluation at infinity. All constructions use incidence, evaluation and unique relative connections, so commute with the specified projective rotations and framing transformations. They therefore give the claimed T-equivariant bijection and all stated invariants, conditional only on the still-unproved absolute GAGA supplier. [A1, F1, F4, F5, step 4.1, step 5.2, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The exact raw equation, Hermitian spaces, polynomial maps and coordinate conventions in the Statement.

[F1] The raw moment maps, stable word span, costability and gauge/framing action have their stated finite-dimensional meanings. [[def-qftx-adhm-linear-data-stability-and-regularity]]

[F2] A constant-rank smooth bundle map has smooth kernel and image subbundles. [[prop-constant-rank-kernels-and-images-of-bundle-maps-over-one-base-are-subbundles]]

[F3] The curvature of a connection is its square, and in a frame is $d\omega+\omega\wedge\omega$. [[def-curvature-of-a-vector-bundle-connection]]

[F4] Commuting complex matrices on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space have a common eigenvector: choose an eigenspace of the first, which is invariant under the second, and then an eigenvector of its restriction. The same applies to dual matrices. [[thm-the-complex-numbers-are-algebraically-closed]]

[F5] The explicit positive stereographic, twistor and real-structure convention is that of the local definition. AC is inherited through the bundle supplier. [[def-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-and-twistor-data]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]



**Given:** The data of the Statement.

1.1 Matrix multiplication gives $b_z^\dagger a_z=(-B_2+z_2)(B_1-z_1)+(B_1-z_1)(B_2-z_2)+IJ=\mu_{\mathbb C}$. Taking adjoints gives the other off-diagonal entry of $DD^\dagger$. Subtracting $a_z^\dagger a_z$ from $b_z^\dagger b_z$ cancels every scalar and linear-in-$z$ term and leaves $[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=\mu_{\mathbb R}$. This proves both identities with their exact signs. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Failure of surjectivity of $b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,B_1-z_1,I)$ gives a nonzero covector $\ell$ with $\ell B_i=z_i\ell$ and $\ell I=0$, contradicting the stable spanning set. Conversely, if the stable word span $S$ is proper, the induced pair on $V/S$ commutes since $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $S$. Its dual has a common eigenvector by [F4], and the resulting covector annihilates $I$ and both rows at the corresponding $z$, so surjectivity fails there. A kernel vector of $a_z$ is a common eigenvector of $B_i$ in $\ker J$ and contradicts costability. Conversely, on any nonzero common invariant $S\subset\ker J$, the pair commutes by the complex equation and has a common eigenvector by [F4], producing such a kernel. This proves both equivalences. [F1, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Expanding $[A,C]+(I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2)(J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)$ gives the stated polynomial with coefficients $\mu_{\mathbb C},\mu_{\mathbb R},-\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. Substitution of $\sigma v$ in $\alpha$, followed by adjoint, gives exactly $(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2)=\beta(v)$. On a real line the same substitution gives $\alpha=a_z\lambda_1+b_z\lambda_2$ and $\beta=b_z^\dagger\lambda_1-a_z^\dagger\lambda_2$. The scalar-coordinate matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\lambda_1&-\bar\lambda_2\\\lambda_2&\bar\lambda_1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is invertible whenever $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\ne0$. Solving the two displayed incidence equations similarly recovers a unique $z$ from each point with $\lambda\ne0$; their real-linear coefficient matrix has determinant $(|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2)^2$. The points with $\lambda=0$ form $L_\infty$. Thus these lines cover $\mathbb P^3$. [F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 At zero real moment, step 1.1 gives $DD^\dagger=\operatorname{diag}(f,f)$ with $f=a^\dagger a=b^\dagger b$. Regularity makes $f$ positive definite by injectivity of $a$, and hence makes $D$ onto. Conversely, surjectivity of $D$ makes both diagonal blocks positive definite; $a$ is injective and $b^\dagger$ onto, so step 2.1 gives regularity. Direct multiplication shows $P^\dagger=P$, $P^2=P$, $DP=0$, and $P$ is the identity on $\ker D$. Inversion of positive matrices is smooth, so [F2] gives the rank-$N$ smooth kernel bundle. Projection of the trivial Hermitian connection is a metric connection because for kernel sections $s,t$, $d\langle s,t\rangle=\langle Pds,t\rangle+\langle s,Pdt\rangle$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Differentiate $DP=0$ and its adjoint to obtain $dP\,P=-D^\dagger(DD^\dagger)^{-1}dD\,P$ and $P\,dP=-P\,dD^\dagger(DD^\dagger)^{-1}D$. Thus [F3] gives $F=P\,dP\wedge dP\,P=P\,dD^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f^{-1},f^{-1})\wedge dD\,P$. Its nonzero differential blocks are $dD=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}dz_2&-dz_1\\-d\bar z_1&-d\bar z_2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The resulting two-form blocks are multiples of $dz_1\wedge d\bar z_1-dz_2\wedge d\bar z_2$, $2dz_1\wedge d\bar z_2$ and $2dz_2\wedge d\bar z_1$, with coefficient $f^{-1}$; the $W$ blocks vanish. Expanding in real coordinates shows that these forms are complex linear combinations of $dx^0\wedge dx^1-dx^2\wedge dx^3$, $dx^0\wedge dx^2+dx^1\wedge dx^3$ and $dx^0\wedge dx^3-dx^1\wedge dx^2$. Each has Hodge star minus itself for the positive Euclidean orientation. Multiplication by the degree-zero matrices $P$ preserves this property, so $F^+=0$. [F3, F5, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 For regular zero-moment data the maps $a_z,b_z$ have orthogonal images and equal positive Gram matrix $f_z$. Therefore $a_z\lambda_1+b_z\lambda_2$ is injective for every nonzero $\lambda$, since its squared norm on $v$ is $(|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2)\langle v,f_zv\rangle$. The identity with $\sigma$ makes $\beta$ surjective as well. At $L_\infty$, $\alpha=(-\mu_1,-\mu_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(\mu_2,-\mu_1,0)$ have the same properties. A nonzero maximal minor locally solves each kernel and image equation by holomorphic matrix inversion, so their kernels, images and middle quotient have holomorphic local frames. Hence the middle cohomology is a holomorphic bundle. On a finite real line, split $K=\operatorname{im}a_z\oplus\operatorname{im}b_z\oplus\ker D_z$. Using $a_z,b_z$ to identify the first two summands with $V\oplus V$, and multiplying the target by $f_z^{-1}$, the first two summands form $V$ copies of the Euler complex $\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)}\mathcal O^2\xrightarrow{(-\lambda_2,\lambda_1)}\mathcal O(1)$, whose middle cohomology is zero. The remaining summand is the constant $\ker D_z$, proving the canonical linewise identification. The identical Euler calculation at infinity leaves $W$ with its standard framing. [F2, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

5.1 Under the stated simultaneous torus transformation, $A$ and $C$ acquire factors $t_1,t_2$ and the third component of $\alpha$ acquires $t_1t_2h$. Dividing the resulting middle map by $t_1t_2$ gives $U_K=\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$, with source factor $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$ and target factor $1$; direct substitution verifies both chain squares. At infinity the Euler blocks cancel and the induced framing action is precisely $h$. This projective torus action preserves the real-line incidence and commutes with $\sigma$ projectively. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, the holomorphic coordinates are $(\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$ with $(\mu_1,\mu_2)=(z_1,z_2)$, so vertical complex orientation followed by the positive stereographic orientation is the complex orientation of $\mathbb P^3$. For $k=0$, $D$ is the unique map to the zero space, $P=1_W$, and all formulas reduce to the framed trivial bundle. No inverse normal-form theorem or global charge calculation was used. [F1, F5, step 2.2, step 4.2, algebra] ∎
